title: Achievements
summary: Every achievement, how to get it and what it pays. Secret ones stay secret.
text: Achievements follow you to every server. Each one pays out once, in the server where you unlock it, from the Reserve. Secret achievements are listed so you know they exist, but not how to get them. Rarities Every achievement FROM THE BOT

title: Who's who
summary: The characters of the Rend-Conomy: Marquez the shopkeeper, TODD the house, and the Connector.
text: The Rend-Conomy has a narrator, and it has a cast. These are the ones you'll meet. Marquez Marquez runs the shop. He's reserved, kind and a little old-fashioned, and he calls you friend, pal, kiddo or champ. He stocks everything from coffee to fishing rods to seeds, buys your fish, crops and Goods, and sets out one collectible a week. He doesn't talk about the Connector. Where: r!shop , r!sellfish , r!sellcrops . TODD TODD is a monitor with opinions. He's the house at the Rend-Sino, the lender of last resort ( r!bailout ), the law when the Underground gets out of hand, and the one who drops into chat with a question and a pot of Polygons. Win ten in a row at his casino and he'll have you escorted out. Ask him to rate something with r!rate ; he'll do it badly. The server's first landmark is a statue of him. The Connector A red suit, a wide red hat, and in its shadow one red eye and one blue. Twitchy, paranoid, speaks in clipped whispers and never says names. He only comes out at night, and he never asks questions. See the Underground .

title: The City
summary: Building on your server's 8×8 map: the twelve buildings, levels, neighbors, tax, freight and train robberies, landmarks, squatters, bids and condemnation.
text: Every server has one map: an 8×8 grid of open land, A1 to H8. Anyone can claim a tile and build on it. Buildings pay rent every day, cost upkeep, wear down, and change the tiles around them. Nobody is capped, but property tax climbs with every building you own, rivals can bid to buy you out, and a place you neglect gets squatters before it falls apart. At a glance Map 8×8, per server Land ⬡1,000 a tile Cheapest building Shack, ⬡2,500 Levels up to 3 Tax-free 1 to 3 buildings TIP A good first building: a Shack next to someone's Park. The Park adds 15% to its rent. See the live map on the city page . Building and upgrading Pick an empty tile and a building: r!property build C4 shack (or just r!build C4 shack ). You pay the building's price plus the land, and construction takes real time; no rent until it's done. Most buildings can be upgraded twice ( r!property upgrade C4 ): rent goes ×1.6, then ×2.4, and the building is fixed up to 100% along the way. Selling or tearing down Sell ( r!property sell C4 ): the bank buys the building and the land for ? of everything that went into it (less if it's run down), and the tile is open land again. Tear down ( r!property teardown C4 park ): knock it down and build something else, keeping the land. The crew pays ? of what went in as salvage, and you pay the new building's price (no land this time). The twelve buildings FROM THE BOT A Lighthouse has to go on the edge of the map, and one Barn is all a farm needs. Neighbors This Shack earns 100% + 15% (Park) − 15% (Factory) + 10% (Station) = 110% rent. "Next door" means the eight tiles around a building, diagonals included. Park next door: +15% rent (up to two Parks). Factory next door: −15% rent and faster wear. Stations, Factories and Warehouses don't mind the smoke. Station within two tiles: +10% rent. Corner Shop: +5% for each home beside it (Shacks, Apartments, Mansions), up to four. Police Station next door: no squatters, and the Connector won't set up within a tile of it. Rent, upkeep and tax Each building pays its rent once a day, scaled by its level, its condition and its neighbors, and charges its upkeep plus property tax on its value. Buildings lose about 2% condition a day (more in storms, next to a Factory, or when you can't pay); repair with r!property repair all . A Lighthouse halves storm damage to all your buildings. What each building does Ballroom: a Mansion owner can throw a party once a day ( r!property party ): chat pay doubles for everyone in the server for an hour. Storefront: pick a player company for your Corner Shop ( r!property storefront C4 TICK ); it earns 10% of the shop's rent, paid by the Reserve. Corner Shops also launder hot loot. Production: a Factory makes 24 crates of Goods a day per level. Sell them to Marquez ( r!property goods sell ) or ship them by freight for more. More Land: a Barn unlocks six more farm plots. Branch Manager: a Bank Branch adds 25% per level to the interest on your savings. Cold Storage: a Warehouse sells your crops at the best price of the last few days. Freight and train robberies Own a finished Station and you can ship your whole crop basket and your Goods by train, once every 6 hours: crops at 15% over market, Goods at ⬡30 a crate. The train takes half an hour. While it's on the rails, any crew can rob it with r!heist train and take up to half of what it carries. Landmarks Build It and They Will Come: the whole server funds landmarks together, one after another, with r!landmark donate <amount> . Donations go into the Reserve, and every finished landmark gives everyone here a perk. The top donor on each one gets Foreman . Squatters, bids and condemnation Squatters: below 40%, squatters can move in. No rent until you evict them ( r!property evict C4 , three days of rent) or repair to 75%. Condemned: at 0% the bank takes the place (paying you a tenth of its value) and auctions it for a day. If nobody bids, it's torn down. Buyout bids: anyone can bid at least 25% over a building's value ( r!property bid C4 <amount> ). The owner has a day to accept or refuse; refusing costs 15% of the bid and shields the building for a week. No answer, and it's sold. Selling: the bank buys any building back for up to 80% of what went into it (less if it's run down) and tears it down.

title: Commands
summary: Every Render Vision command, by section, with its aliases and slash form. Filter by name or what it does.
text: Every command works as r!command or as a slash command. Words in <angle brackets> are needed; words in [square brackets] are optional. Moderator commands share one slash command, /mod . Press / anywhere on the wiki to search. Every command FROM THE BOT

title: Player companies
summary: Found your own company, grow it level by level, take it public on the exchange, pay yourself, and defend it from hostile takeovers.
text: Any player can found a company. It has a treasury, levels up as you invest, and at level 3 it can go public: other players can buy its shares, and it gets its own page on the exchange . At a glance Founding ⬡2,500, approved by mods Go public at level 3 Listing fee ⬡2,000 Shares 1,000 ( 400 for sale) Founding one r!found TICK Your Company Name sends it to the server's moderators for approval; if the name is rejected you get your money back. Once approved, that money becomes the company's treasury. See it with r!company . The treasury grows when you invest ( r!invest ), when players work there (every shift adds half the worker's pay, and anyone can r!apply TICK ), and from share sales after it goes public. Levels Upgrades are paid from the treasury ( r!upgrade ). Every level costs upkeep each day, and raises what the company can pay. Going public At level 3 (Firm), r!ipo lists the company. Anyone but the owner can then buy and sell its shares, and the first 400 shares sold fund the company. Its price moves with trading, and its treasury earns from revenue: farmers' market sales, a Corner Shop's Storefront on the city map, and more. Once it's public, your employees' pay follows the share price like a house company's: double the IPO price and shifts pay double, from ? × up to ? × the normal pay. You can pay yourself a salary of up to 10% of the treasury a day ( r!salary ), but the stock dips when you do. Upkeep and closing The treasury pays upkeep every day. Miss a payment and the market panics; keep missing them and the price slides to zero and the company closes for good, taking every share with it. A private company closes after missing upkeep three days in a row. Closing it yourself r!closecompany shows what you'd get; r!closecompany confirm does it. A public company first buys out every shareholder at the share price, from the treasury and then your wallet if the treasury runs short. You get what's left of the treasury minus a ? closing fee. The levels you paid for are gone, employees lose their jobs, and you can't found another company for ? days. Selling it r!sellcompany @player <price> offers the whole company (treasury, level and staff) to another player in your server. They have a day to answer with r!sellcompany accept or decline ; r!sellcompany cancel takes it back. The buyer can't already run a company, and has to sell any shares they hold in it first. No sale while a takeover bid is open. Takeovers and mergers Hostile takeover: a player who holds at least half of the shares for sale can bid for your company with r!takeover , putting up a premium of a quarter of its worth. You have a day to answer; no answer and it goes through. Poison pill: defend for a tenth of the company's worth ( r!takeover defend ). The bidder gets their premium back minus a 20% break fee, which goes to you, and your company is shielded from takeovers for 7 days. Merger: two owners can agree to merge with r!merge .

title: Emojis
summary: All of the bot's pixel-art emojis, by group, with their names.
text: The bot draws its own emojis: 128-pixel art on a 32-pixel grid, each in a frame with its section's color. They show up in the bot's replies and across the site. An item's emoji is named after the item. Every emoji FROM THE BOT

title: Events
summary: World events that change the game for an hour, and what happens in December.
text: World events FROM THE BOT Every few hours, one of these runs for an hour in every server. r!event shows the one running now. December: Polygon Holidays The advent calendar ( r!advent ): a door a day from December 1 to 25. Missed doors open late. Polygons, seeds, items and collectibles, and something special behind the last door. Secret Santa ( r!santa ): sign up by December 14. On the 15th everyone who joined is matched up; wrap a gift of Polygons and an item, and it's delivered on Christmas Day. The holiday shelf: Marquez stocks December-only collectibles and paints. Snow Day: a December event with no work but double chat pay. In October, pumpkins sell for 25% more.

title: Everyday money
summary: The daily allowance, chat pay, TODD's drop-ins, savings accounts, loans between players, gifts, trades, your inbox, profile and leaderboards.
text: The daily allowance r!daily pays ⬡250 once per day; the day turns over at midnight Eastern. Claim it every day to build a streak. Chat pay and drop-ins Talking in the server pays ⬡5 to ⬡15 a message, once a minute, up to ⬡300 a day. Very short messages don't count. Now and then TODD drops in with a question and a pot of Polygons for whoever answers first. A Mansion party, the Stadium landmark and the Gossip Hour event all raise chat pay. Savings Lock Polygons away and get them back with interest: r!savings deposit 1000 7 . Up to 3 accounts and ⬡50,000 in all, from ⬡100 each. A Bank Branch on the city map adds 25% per level to your interest. Loans From TODD: r!bailout when you're nearly broke: ⬡500 now, ⬡600 owed. No gambling until it's paid ( r!repay ). From another player: r!loan @player 1000 5 asks for ⬡1,000 at 5% a day (up to 25%); they accept or decline. Loans are due in a week. Overdue, and half of what you earn from work, dailies and dividends goes to the lender until it's paid. r!loans lists yours; a lender can r!forgive . Gifts and trades Gifts: r!gift @player 500 sends Polygons with a 5% fee, up to ⬡5,000 a day. Trades: offer Polygons and/or an item for someone else's ( r!trade @player 500 for rod ). What you offer is held safely until they answer; offers expire in a day (you get it back), and you can have three open. Your inbox r!inbox collects what happened while you were away: receipts, price alerts, bids on your buildings, ready crops, trade offers. On the site, the bell in the top bar shows new ones. r!receipts on also sends receipts by DM. Profile and leaderboards A Title item sets the line under your name ( r!settitle ); r!settitle clear removes it. r!profile shows your net worth, achievements and pinned showcase ( r!showcase ). Customize its color, theme, banner and frame, or edit it on your profile page on the site. r!leaderboard ranks the server by net worth, Polygons or shifts. Playing from the site Log in with Discord on the Play hub to work, farm, build, trade and read your inbox from a browser, and open the Trading Floor Activity right inside Discord.

title: Farming
summary: Seeds, planting, watering and harvesting; crop grades and daily prices; mutations; more plots and the Barn; Fertilizer; and the farmhand.
text: Every server gives you a small farm. Buy seeds from Marquez, plant them, water them once per stage, and harvest when they're ready. Crops grow in real time, even while you're away. Sell your basket to Marquez, at the farmers' market, or by freight . At a glance Plots 3 to start, up to 15 Wilts after 12 thirsty hours Farmhand ⬡150 a day Crops r!plant carrot fills every empty plot (or r!plant corn 2 for just plot 2); then r!water and r!harvest . Tomatoes keep producing: after the first harvest they regrow twice, in half the time. Pumpkins are worth 25% more in October. TIP Crows can eat a crop (a Scarecrow keeps them off), and Storm events can flatten crops outside a Greenhouse. Rain waters everything for free. Quality grades Every crop is graded the moment it's harvested. Its grade sets the range its price is rolled from when you sell it: each one is rolled separately, so a basket of the same crop sells for a little more or less every time. Harvest a Prime crop for Quality Control , and a Prime crop that's also Golden or Rainbow for Cream of the Crop . Daily prices On top of grades, every crop's price moves each day, between 80% and 120% of normal, the same for everyone. r!farm prices shows today's. A Warehouse on the city map lets you sell at the best price of the last 3 days (5 at level 2, 7 at level 3). Mutations Now and then a crop comes out special, and worth far more: Selling To Marquez: r!sellcrops sells your whole basket. At the farmers' market: r!sellcrops TICK sells to a player company for 10% more, and the company earns a cut (not your own company). By freight: with a Station on the city map, ship the basket for 15% over market. See freight . More plots and the Barn Buy plots one at a time with r!buyplot . Past nine, you need a Barn on the city map , which unlocks six more. The farm always shows three rows: three plots across, or five with a Barn. Fertilizer Fertilizer makes a crop grow 50% faster and come out Prime more often. r!fertilize works it into every growing crop at once, as far as your Fertilizer goes, or r!fertilize 3 for one plot. Buy it from Marquez or make it from fishing junk with r!compost . The farmhand Hire him with r!farmhand hire for ⬡150 a day. While you're away he waters everything, harvests each crop the moment it's ready, and replants from his seed shed (the same crop as before, or what he has most of). He never buys seeds: stock his shed with r!farmhand give carrot 20 . Give him Fertilizer too ( r!farmhand give fertilizer 10 ) and he works one into every crop he plants. When you open your farm, he tells you what he did while you were gone. He DMs you when he runs out of seeds (turn that off with r!farmhand dms off ). If you can't pay him, he quits and leaves the shed with you. He doesn't sell your crops; that's still your call.

title: Your first day
summary: Join, claim a daily, work a shift, and what Polygons are. Everything a new player needs in the first ten minutes.
text: The Rend-Conomy is the economy game inside Render Vision, the Render Productions Discord bot. You earn Polygons (written ⬡), spend them, invest them, and occasionally lose them in spectacular ways. Every server has its own economy: your balance in one server has nothing to do with another. Your achievements follow you everywhere. At a glance You start with ⬡500 Daily allowance ⬡250 Resets 12 AM Eastern Prefix r! or / Joining There's nothing to sign up for. The first command you use creates your account with ⬡500 . Every command works as r!command or as a slash command ( /command ); r!help lists them by section, and the commands page lists every one. Your first ten minutes Claim your daily: r!daily pays ⬡250 once per day (Eastern time). Keep a streak going for the achievements. Get a job: r!apply RRM (or NACH, BLU, BNW, BSTG). Then r!work every 15 minutes. Each shift gives you a quick task; type the answer in the channel. See Work . Do a gig between shifts: r!gig needs no job and works every 10 minutes. r!oddjob gives you up to 10 more small jobs a day. Look around the shop: r!shop opens Marquez's shelves. A Fishing Rod or some seeds are good first buys. Check your money: r!bal shows everything you have, what you owe, and your net worth. TIP Just talking in the server earns Polygons too: a few for each message (one a minute counts), up to ⬡300 a day. Spamming doesn't help. Where Polygons come from Almost every payout in the game, from shifts to rent to casino wins, is paid out of the Polygon Reserve , a single pot shared by everyone. Almost everything you spend goes back into it. That's worth understanding early, because it's the reason payouts can shrink. If you go broke TODD will lend you ⬡500 with r!bailout when you have less than ⬡100 , and you'll owe him ⬡600 . While you owe TODD, the Rend-Sino won't let you gamble. Pay him back with r!repay . Where to go next Read about the Reserve , then pick a path . Achievements are a great guide to what's possible: r!achievements shows yours, and every one pays out the first time.

title: Fishing
summary: Casting, bait and lures, using fish as bait for bigger fish, every catch and what Marquez pays for it, and the odds of each cast.
heads: Bait, lures and fish as bait
text: Buy a Fishing Rod from Marquez and cast with r!fish . Each cast costs a little bait unless you have a Lure on. You might catch nothing, snag your line, pull up junk, find a lost wallet, or land a fish. Sell your bag with r!sellfish . At a glance Cast every 3 min Bait ⬡5 A Lure lasts 25 casts Bag holds 50 Bait, lures and fish as bait Plain bait is the cheapest way to fish. A Lure makes bigger fish more likely. Better still, a fish you've caught makes good bait for the next size up: r!fish perch . Carrots from your farm work like a small fish. What you can catch Use a fish as bait and catch a bigger one for There's Always a Bigger Fish , and land the White Whale for Moby Dick . Perks A Shack on the city map gives you free bait (Bait Shed). A Lighthouse makes plain bait fish like a Lure (Beacon). The Fish Frenzy event lets you cast every 90 seconds, and plain bait works like a Lure.

title: Bait, lures and fish as bait
Glossary
summary: Short definitions of the words the Rend-Conomy uses: Heat, escrow, the payout factor, net worth and more.
text: Terms Polygons (⬡) The currency. Every server has its own Polygons. The Reserve The house's pot of Polygons: almost every payout comes from it and most spending goes back in. More . Payout factor The share of a payout that's actually paid. 100% normally; lower when the Reserve is under a quarter full. Net worth Everything you have: Polygons, savings, shares, buildings, minus what you owe. Escrow Polygons held safely by the bot while something is undecided, like a bid or a trade. You get them back if it falls through. Shift One round of work at your job: a task, then pay. Every 15 minutes. Rush A bonus task right after a shift, which only pays if you get it right. Dividends What shares earn while you hold them. Short A bet that a stock will fall. Limit / stop order An order to buy or sell automatically when a price is reached. Grade A crop's quality: Poor, Fine or Prime. It sets the range its price is rolled from. Mutation A rare crop that comes out Golden, Rainbow or Square and is worth many times more. Tile One square of a server's 8×8 city map, named like C4. Condition How well kept a building is, 0–100%. Rent scales with it. Squatters People living in a neglected building. No rent until they're gone. Condemned A building that fell to 0%. The bank takes it and auctions it. Freight Shipping your crops and Goods by train from your Station. Goods Crates a Factory makes. Sell them to Marquez or ship them. Landmark A big building the whole server funds together, with a perk for everyone. VIP Your Rend-Sino level, from everything you've ever bet. Comes with a daily free spin. Progressive jackpot A pot every bet in the server adds to. Three diamonds on Slots win it. Heat How much attention you've drawn from TODD, 0–100 (five stars). High Heat gets you raided. Contraband What the Connector sells: items that bend the rules. Hot loot Stolen valuables from heists. Fence or launder them before they get you caught. World event A change that runs for an hour in every server, like Happy Hour or a Storm.

title: Heists
summary: Plan a heist with a crew of three to five: targets, roles and their odds, stakes, hauls, fines, and robbing freight trains.
text: Someone plans a heist in a channel, others join with a role, and when the leader starts it everyone pays a stake. Then it plays out. A clean job splits the haul evenly; a failed one loses the stakes, and if TODD catches the crew, there's a fine on top. At a glance Crew 3 to 5 Per player one every 6 hours Per server one an hour Targets r!heist vault , stash , reserve or train . Hauls come out of the Reserve, so robbing it really does hurt everyone. Roles Pick a role when you join. Each one adds to the crew's odds: Robbing a train When a Station owner ships freight on the city map , the train spends half an hour on open track. A crew can rob it in that window and take up to half of what it carries. The owner still gets the rest when it arrives. You can't rob your own train. Hot loot A clean heist sometimes drops hot loot for each crew member: a ring, a painting, a gem or a crate. It's worth a lot, but holding it draws Heat. Fence it or launder it through the Underground . TIP A Lockpick Set adds 15% to your next heist, and the Police Strike event adds 15% for everyone for an hour.

title: Items
summary: Everything Marquez sells, by shelf, with prices, stock and what each item does, plus the weekly collectibles.
text: Marquez's shelves restock every hour, and his stock is shared by every server, so popular items can sell out. One collectible is on sale each week, one per customer. Buy with r!purchase <item> [amount] and use with r!use <item> [amount] ; items marked "works on its own" do their thing just by being in your inventory. Using lots at once: r!use mystery 10 or r!use mystery all opens up to ? in one message. Coffee, the Customizer Kit, the Megaphone, paints and the Rush Order go one at a time. Rush Order: r!use rush order coffee has Marquez restock that one item to full, for everyone. Not for collectibles, and you keep the Rush Order if the item is already full. Selling back: r!sellitem <item> [amount|all] . Marquez pays ? of his current price and puts it back on his shelf. He doesn't buy collectibles (trade those with r!trade ), and fish and crops have their own buyers. Throwing away: r!discard <item> [amount|all] , for nothing. Every item FROM THE BOT

title: The Market
summary: Shares in the five house companies: buying and selling, dividends, limit and stop orders, brokers and short selling.
text: Five house companies trade on the Rend-Conomy market, and their prices move all day on their own. Buy shares, hold them for dividends, sell them higher, or bet against them. Prices are the same in every server; your shares belong to the server you bought them in. Starting prices RRM · Render Room ⬡167 NACH · De Nacho ⬡120 BNW · Business Numbers Working ⬡80 BSTG · Bastardly Glory ⬡75 BLU · Builder's League United ⬡47 Trading hours You can trade from 3 AM to 9 PM Eastern , every day. Overnight the market is after hours: prices still drift (a quarter as much), but nobody can buy or sell, and orders and brokers wait for the open. Now and then TODD halts trading on a company or the whole market after a big move. Buying and selling r!market shows every price; r!chart RRM draws the last day; r!compare puts them side by side. Buy with r!buy RRM 10 (or an amount of Polygons) and sell with r!sell RRM all . Big trades move the price against you a little. The live prices are also on the market page . Bastardly Glory is the wild one: it can soar, and it can crash. Goals and news Companies announce goals in the market news. Hit the goal and the stock jumps; miss it and it drops, and nobody knows the result ahead of time. Watch for breaking news, rumors that may or may not be true, and the odd story that shakes the whole market at once. Every company has good stretches and bad ones, and no stretch lasts forever. The Rend Times from Marquez's shop drops vague hints. Dividends Companies pay dividends per share as they do well. Every share you hold earns its part while you hold it; collect what's built up with r!dividends . Limit and stop orders Orders fill on their own while you're away ( r!order ): Limit buy: buy a number of shares once the price falls to your limit. The money is set aside until it fills. Limit sell: sell once the price rises to your target. Stop: sell once the price falls to your stop, to cut a loss. Up to 10 open at once; they expire after 7 days. Brokers A broker trades for you by rules you set ( r!broker ), for a daily salary and a cut of the profit. Each has a style: Short selling Think a stock will fall? r!short BSTG 20 bets on it: you profit by however much it drops, and lose by however much it rises. Opening one holds half its value as margin, plus a 1% fee, and you can short up to 100 shares of a company. If your loss reaches 90% of the margin, the short is closed for you. r!cover closes one. If a company goes bankrupt, every short on it pays out in full. TIP The Bear Rumors and Fire Sale events make shorts free to open for an hour.

title: The odds
summary: Every Rend-Sino game's payouts and expected return, the jackpot, VIP levels, and the odds of heists and fishing.
text: Every number here comes straight from the code, so it's exactly what the games do. "Expected return" is what a game pays back on average for every ⬡100 bet: 96% means you lose ⬡4 per ⬡100 over the long run. Rend-Sino games FROM THE BOT VIP levels Heists The base odds of each target; each role in the crew adds its bonus on top. Fishing Crop grades and mutations

title: Picking a path
summary: Trader, farmer, landlord, gambler or crook: what each way of playing is like, what it costs to start and where to read more.
text: There's no class to pick and you can do everything at once. But most players lean one way. Here's what each path feels like, roughly from the safest to the wildest. The worker Shifts every 15 minutes, gigs every 10, odd jobs and promotions. Steady, needs you to be around, and the pay follows your company's share price. Start: r!apply . Work → The farmer Buy seeds, plant, water, harvest, sell. Crops grow in real time from 30 minutes to a day, come out Poor, Fine or Prime, and sometimes mutate into something worth five or twelve times as much. Hire a farmhand and it runs while you're away. Start: seeds from r!shop garden , then r!farm . Farming → The angler A Fishing Rod and a few Polygons of bait per cast. Small fish make good bait for bigger ones, and somewhere out there is the White Whale. Start: a Rod from r!shop tackle , then r!fish . Fishing → The trader Buy and sell shares in the five house companies (and players' companies), collect dividends, set limit and stop orders, hire a broker, or short a stock you think will fall. Start: r!market . The Market → · Player companies → The landlord Claim tiles on your server's city map and build: Shacks, shops, Stations, Factories, Mansions. Rent comes in daily; upkeep, tax, neighbors and rivals' buyout bids keep it interesting. Start: ⬡1,000 of land plus a building. The City → The gambler The Rend-Sino: slots, blackjack, roulette, the Rocket and more, a progressive jackpot, and VIP levels with a free spin a day. Every game's odds are published, and win ten in a row and TODD throws you out. The Rend-Sino → The crook Heists with a crew, and at night, the Connector's black market: contraband, hot loot, smuggling and snitching. Every shady move adds Heat, and Heat gets you raided. Heists → · The Underground →

title: The Rend-Sino
summary: Every Rend-Sino game, the progressive jackpot, VIP levels and free spins, the multiplayer blackjack table, Happy Hour and TODD's hot-streak rule.
text: TODD's casino. Every game's odds are published and match the code exactly ( the odds ), the house keeps a small, honest edge, and wins are paid from the Reserve . Bets start at ⬡10 . At a glance Minimum bet ⬡10 Jackpot starts at ⬡10,000 Hot-streak limit 10 wins VIP levels 5 The games Plus three that work differently: Ride the Bus ( r!bus ): four card guesses in a row, cash out any time after the first. The Polygon Derby ( r!derby ): start a race, everyone in the channel bets on a horse, and it runs live. The lottery ( r!lottery ): tickets are ⬡50 (up to 20 a week), and the pot is drawn every Sunday at 8 PM Eastern. Lose a spin on Slots and you get Redeem yourself : one free spin of 15 reels, and seven of a kind wins your bet back. The progressive jackpot Every bet in the server adds 1% to the jackpot ( 3% during Happy Hour). Three 💎 on Slots win it: all of it at the maximum Slots bet, a share of it below (bet half the max, win half the jackpot). Then it starts over from ⬡10,000 . r!jackpot shows how big it is. VIP and free spins VIP levels come from everything you've ever bet in the server. Each level comes with a free Slots spin every day ( r!vip spin ): win and it's paid, lose and it cost nothing. Free spins can hit the jackpot too. The blackjack table r!table 100 opens a table in the channel. Up to five players press Sit down , the host presses Deal , and everyone pays the stake. Hands are played in turn with Hit, Stand and Double; each player has 45 seconds before TODD stands for them. Then TODD plays his hand and every seat is paid like solo blackjack. Win at a table of three or more for House Party . Happy Hour A world event that comes around now and then: the jackpot grows three times as fast, VIPs get a second free spin, and TODD looks the other way on hot streaks. TODD's rules Hot streaks: win 10 games in a row and TODD has you escorted out for 3 hours. A Fake ID from the Connector gets you back in. No gambling while you owe TODD for a bailout. A game left unfinished for two minutes is forfeited. One moment between games. LOADED DICE The Connector sells Loaded Dice that improve your odds for a few games. TODD sometimes notices. See the Underground .

title: The Polygon Reserve
summary: The single pot every payout comes from and most spending goes back to, and why payouts shrink when it runs low.
text: The Polygon Reserve is the house's money. Shifts, gigs, rent, dividends, fish sales, casino wins and achievement payouts all come out of it. Shop purchases, bets, upkeep, fees and fines go back in. It's shared by every server, so how everyone plays affects everyone. At a glance Full size ⬡25,000,000 Payouts shrink below 25% Lowest payouts 10% When payouts shrink While the Reserve holds more than a quarter of its full size, every payout is paid in full. Below that, payouts shrink in step with it: at an eighth full, you get half; they never drop below a tenth. Your r!bal and most payout messages say when this is happening, and r!reserve shows exactly how full it is. WHY A shrinking payout is the economy's brake: it stops the house from paying out money it doesn't have. Helping it Spending puts Polygons back: the shop, upkeep, bets, the farmhand's wage. Donations: r!reserve donate <amount> . The top five patrons are listed in r!reserve , and there are achievements for it. Landmarks: money donated to a landmark goes into the Reserve too. Hurting it A heist on the Reserve takes straight from it, so robbing it really does cost everyone. Big casino wins and achievement payouts drain it too, which is why every game's odds are published and fair rather than generous.

title: The Underground
summary: The Connector's black market: when and where he sets up, passwords, contraband, hot loot, laundering, smuggling, snitching, Heat and raids.
text: Every night from 10 PM to 4 AM Eastern , a figure in a red suit sets up somewhere on your server's city map. The Connector sells things Marquez won't, buys things nobody should, and never asks questions. Everything shady you do adds Heat , and Heat gets you raided. At a glance Open 10 PM–4 AM Eastern Command r!ug Heat 0–100, five stars Where he sets up He squats in a condemned building if there is one; otherwise in the most run-down place on the map (its owner loses half that day's rent); otherwise on an empty lot. He won't set up within a tile of a Police Station. If stations cover the whole map, he takes an alley off the map instead: there's always a password that night, and every deal there brings 50% more Heat. Password nights About one night in three, you need a password to get in. From 8 PM, the Connector hijacks one of TODD's drop-ins to leave it, hidden in a spoiler. Get in with r!ug <password> . Contraband Four of these are for sale each night ( r!ug buy <item> ): Hot loot Clean heists sometimes drop hot loot. Holding it adds Heat every day. Fence it ( r!ug fence ): half its value when it's fresh, rising to 90% after three days. Launder it through a Corner Shop you own ( r!ug launder ): its full value, a day later. Smuggling Once a night, put up between ⬡500 and ⬡10,000 ( r!ug smuggle <amount> ). Two hours later it comes back with 50% on top, 10% on top, or not at all (caught, with a lot of Heat). A Lighthouse lowers the chance of getting caught. Snitching For ⬡250 , tip TODD off about another player ( r!ug snitch @player ). If they're at three stars or more, they're raided and you get a reward plus a share of their fine. If not, the Heat lands on you. Heat and raids Heat runs from 0 to 100, shown as stars, and cools by 10 a day. The more stars, the more likely a raid: TODD confiscates your contraband and loot and fines you a tenth of your Polygons (up to ⬡5,000). At 100 Heat you're locked out for two nights. r!ug heat shows yours.

title: Work
summary: Jobs at the five house companies: shifts every 15 minutes, rush tasks, reviews and promotions, gigs and odd jobs.
text: Every house company on the market is also an employer. Get hired, work a shift every 15 minutes, answer the task it gives you, and climb from the bottom rank to the top. Your pay follows your company's share price, so a booming company pays better. Player companies are employers too: their pay follows their level, and their share price once they're public (see Player companies ). At a glance Shift every 15 min Gig every 10 min Base pay ⬡35 Ranks 4 per company The jobs Apply with r!apply <ticker> . Each company has its own kind of task and its own four ranks; the multiplier after each rank is how much more it pays than the first. Shifts and tasks r!work hands you a task: sort a mod queue, build a nacho order, put building steps in order, crunch numbers, spot a bug. Type the answer in the channel. You have about 20 seconds. Right and fast: full pay, plus a tip of up to 50% for speed. Wrong or too slow: you still get 40% . Rush: after a right answer there's a 20% chance another task comes in (up to 5 in a row). Rush tasks pay only if they're right. Coworkers: people working in the same channel within two minutes add 15% each (up to 3 ). Pay: ⬡35 × the company's price compared to where it started × your rank. Bastardly Glory's swings are capped so its pay stays sane. r!job shows your rank, accuracy, next review and next shift; r!job remind on pings you when a shift is ready. Reviews and promotions Every 10 shifts you get a review. Get 8 or more right and you're promoted; 4 or fewer and you're demoted. A great review at the top rank pays a bonus instead. You can quit 24 hours after being hired ( r!quit ), and you keep your rank if you come back. LAYOFFS If your company goes bankrupt, you're laid off with a few shifts' pay. A Hard Hat from Marquez keeps your job through one layoff. Gigs and odd jobs Gigs ( r!gig ): no job needed, every 10 minutes, pays 40% of a first-rank shift. Begging ( r!beg ): once an hour. ? of the time someone gives you ⬡ ? – ? , ? a cheap item from Marquez's shelf, otherwise nothing. Rich beggars get noticed: from a net worth of ? there's a ? chance you're caught ( ? from ? , ? from ? ). Then TODD fines you ? of your wallet (at most ? ), or Marquez just tells you off. Odd jobs ( r!oddjob ): a math problem, an unscramble, a count or a reverse. Answer in the channel within 90 seconds; up to 10 a day. Items that help Coffee resets your work cooldown. Overtime makes your next shift pay double. Hard Hat keeps your job through one layoff. Look out for the Labor Shortage and Hiring Spree world events , which raise pay for an hour.
